parsed.explanation: No traveller-facing restriction is documented: entry and screening follow the parent's federal regime, which the dossier presents without hostile rules; there is no presentation offence (sodomy statute replaced), no facility or custody ban, and no trans-specific violence record. The territory has an operative human-rights statute covering gender identity, extended by a 2017 official interpretation to trans students, plus marriage access visitors can rely on — documented protections, though not demonstrated through enforcement outcomes. The thin record leaves open questions (custody placement, violence prevalence, whether the statute produces real remedies), which under the rubric weigh far less than exposures. Extrapolating from protective law, federal screening, and absent documented hostility resolves above the acceptance-with-protections tier's lower edge but below jurisdictions with proven enforcement, at reduced risk.
